It has been revealed that babies are not cheap! You'll be blowing through roughly 240 to 360 diapers a month. Here are some ways you can save:.

Prioritize fit and leak protection.

Make your diaper budget work for you. Fewer leaks and blowouts mean fewer outfit changes (and fewer middle-of-the-night sheet swaps). So, the convenience alone will pay for itself. You don’t even have to trade up to a premium line to get it: Mainstream Pampers lines like Swaddlers and Baby Dry cover the pediatric-aligned basics. Store-brand diapers offer a lower-cost option for budget-conscious parents.

In a recent development, if your baby's skin isn't super reactive, there’s no need to splurge on specialty wipes. A fragrance-free, alcohol-free sensitive-skin wipe'll do the trick.

Weigh a subscription vs. buying separately.

Here are five picks, drilled down by category:.

What are the best newborn care essentials to buy before the baby arrives?

Stick to the basics: a safe sleep surface, an infant car seat, diapering supplies (diapers, wipes, barrier cream, and a changing surface), a few onesies, and whatever your feeding initiative requires. Everything else can wait.

Should I get sensitive-skin wipes or water wipes for newborn diaper changes?

Industry observers note that fragrance-free, alcohol-free sensitive wipes meet pediatric guidance for everyday newborn use. Water wipes are an extra-cautious option for babies who have eczema-prone or very reactive skin.

What newborn essentials are best for preventing diaper rash from day one?

In a recent development, two non-negotiables: Change diapers frequently and use a zinc-oxide or petrolatum-based barrier cream. A well-fitting, absorbent diaper helps too.

Should I prioritize premium diapers or sensitive wipes in my newborn essentials budget?

It has been revealed that prioritize diaper fit and leak protection first, since that’s what keeps moisture off skin (and blowouts off clothes). Then save on wipes: A fragrance-free, alcohol-free sensitive wipe covers most babies without specialty pricing.

Is a diaper subscription bundle or buying essentials separately a better value for newborns?

Sources indicate that this is really a convenience-vs-flexibility call. Diaper subscription bundles offer discounts the more you buy and can spare you store runs. Buying separately lets you switch sizes as your baby grows — which happens fast in the newborn stage!

What are the best newborn care essentials to buy in 2026?

Recent findings suggest that the same ones as always. The core list (sleep surface, car seat, diapering, clothes, and feeding) hasn’t changed in 2026; there are just more options. You still need a snug/leakproof diaper, fragrance-free wipes, a zinc-oxide barrier cream, and a portable changing pad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal jury in the District of Maryland convicted a laboratory owner yesterday for taking advantage of nursing homes that needed COVID-19 tests during the pandemic and fraudulently billing Medicare more than $18 million for other expensive respiratory tests that nursing home residents did not need, physicians did not order, and, in many cases, were never performed.
  • Britton-Harr’s decision to exploit elderly nursing‑home residents and inexperienced interns for personal gain during a global pandemic is unconscionable.
  • Recent findings suggest that “This verdict sends a clear message: the FBI will aggressively pursue anyone who steals from American taxpayers,” said FBI Baltimore Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal jury in the District of Maryland convicted a laboratory owner yesterday for taking advantage of nursing homes that needed COVID-19 tests during the pandemic and fraudulently billing Medicare more than $18 million for other expensive respiratory tests that nursing home residents did not need, physicians did not order, and, in many cases, were never performed.

“Mr. Britton-Harr’s decision to exploit elderly nursing‑home residents and inexperienced interns for personal gain during a global pandemic is unconscionable. This verdict reinforces our message: there is nowhere to hide for those who commit fraud. We will find you and prosecute you to the fullest extent of the law,” noted U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes for the District of Maryland. “The U.S. Attorney’s Office, along with our law-enforcement partners, remains committed to rooting out fraud and holding accountable those who exploit our vulnerable victims and who steal our taxpayer money.”.

Recent findings suggest that “This verdict sends a clear message: the FBI will aggressively pursue anyone who steals from American taxpayers,” said FBI Baltimore Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul. “Patrick Britton-Harr will now face the consequences of his greed and brazen crimes. In addition to this healthcare fraud scheme, Britton-Harr was previously convicted for investment fraud in which the FBI uncovered a separate scheme where he defrauded private citizens. The FBI and our law enforcement partners will not rest until fraudsters like Mr. Britton Harr are brought to justice.”.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Patrick Britton-Harr, 42, of Annapolis, offered COVID-19 tests to nursing homes across the country in 2020 when these facilities were desperate for COVID-19 testing services. After specimens were collected from nursing home residents and other laboratories performed COVID-19 testing, Britton-Harr billed Medicare for separate, high-priced respiratory pathogen panel (RPP) tests purportedly conducted in a laboratory he owned in Arizona. Britton-Harr falsely claimed to Medicare that treating physicians ordered these extensive RPP tests, which screened for more than 30 respiratory pathogens. In reality, physicians never ordered the tests for their nursing home patients, and several physicians testified at trial they had never ordered an RPP test for any patient during the entirety of their medical careers.

In a recent development, through his firm, Provista Health, Britton-Harr fraudulently billed Medicare $18.7 million for RPP testing purportedly performed in just six months, of which Medicare paid more than $7.2 million. Evidence at trial demonstrated how Britton-Harr exploited inexperienced employees, including a family member and high school and college aged interns, by directing them to bill Medicare for an RPP test every time a COVID-19 test was performed. Britton-Harr further directed the billing of RPP tests supposedly performed at his Arizona laboratory after he had already closed the laboratory, barred staff from working in the laboratory, and no longer had the equipment necessary to run RPP tests. Additional evidence at trial proved that Britton-Harr billed Medicare for RPP tests that were never performed, including billing for tests for nursing home residents who were already deceased.

Britton-Harr used the proceeds of his fraud scheme to fund a lavish lifestyle, purchasing, among other things, a $112,500 Porsche 911, and making $25,000 monthly mortgage payments on his Annapolis waterfront mansion.

It has been revealed that the jury convicted Britton-Harr of five counts of health care fraud and one count of transactional money laundering. Britton-Harr faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for each count. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled at a later date. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

HHS-OIG and FBI investigated the case.

Recent findings suggest that trial Attorney Chris Wenger of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Ari Evans for the District of Maryland are prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice confirmed the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, at the moment comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, catster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission at no cost to you. Learn more.

Cats = happiness. Itâs an equation that neither cat lovers nor the cats themselves will find surprising, but itâs not something you expect to be evaluated, let alone proven, through scientific research. In a recent correlational study of subjective well-being across 93 countries, researchers examined the relationship between cat density, exposure to Toxoplasma gondii, socioeconomic status, and national happiness, with interesting results.

According to the study, countries with more pet cats tend to report higher happiness levels, a discovery that some news and social media headlines have taken a little out of context. The key word in this study is correlational. Researchers have not discovered that happiness levels are the result of larger feline populations â ie, a causal relationship â only that there is a notable connection between countries reporting higher numbers of pet cats and those ranked highest on the World Population Reviewâs 2025 report on the Happiest Countries in the World.

So before you trade your antidepressant prescription for a kitten, there are a few things worth understanding.

Apparently, Cats Are Good for the National Mood.

The researchers found a positive correlation between estimated cat density and national happiness scores. In plain English, countries with more cats tended to report higher happiness levels.

Recent findings suggest that interesting? Absolutely. Proof that cats make people happier? Not quite.

The study compared data from entire countries rather than following individuals before and after they adopted a cat. So it cannot tell whether cats improve happiness, happier people are more likely to keep cats, or something else is going on.

Recent findings suggest that we know that pet cats offer companionship and amazing moments of genuine connection. They somehow have the ability to draw a smile on our face without saying a single word, simply by lying on our lap or sitting beside us after a difficult day. Emotional support comes in many forms, and cats seem to know just the right way to make us feel happier, calmer, and more at ease.

In a recent development, but personal experience and national statistics are two different things. A purring companion can brighten someone's day; proving that cats raise an entire country's happiness score takes considerably more evidence.

Hereâs where the story gets interesting. Not too surprisingly, economic prosperity had a stronger relationship with happiness than cat density. The relationship between national income and happiness had a Pearson correlation coefficient of around 0.80, compared with 0.62 for cat numbers.

In other words, a country's wealth was more closely associated with how happy its people reported feeling than the estimated number of cats living there. Money certainly doesn't guarantee happiness, but it can definitely make life less stressful when we compare it with living with no resources.

Financial security can help afford nutritious food, veterinary visits, pay the rent, and have the peace of mind of being able to cover unexpected medical bills. Access to healthcare, personal safety, and stable living conditions are notable too.

Sources indicate that this wider picture could help explain why cat density and happiness move together. The relationship might reflect the broader social environment rather than some magical feline effect.

Recent findings suggest that cats can enrich our lives, absolutely. But even the most accomplished biscuit-maker cannot fix unaffordable housing. And a cat's approach to financial planning remains questionable at best. Knocking an expensive object off a shelf to demand dinner is hardly a sustainable economic strategy.

The researchers also examined Toxoplasma gondii, a parasite that reproduces in cats and other felids.

Countries with more people showing signs of a recent infection tended to have lower happiness scores. To explore this, researchers considered two types of antibodies: one that can sometimes indicate a more recent infection and another generally associated with past exposure. Neither provides a perfect timeline of when the infection occurred.

Thereâs another important detail. The researchers used infection estimates from pregnant women, and that may not accurately represent the entire population.

Sources indicate that most importantly, the study does not prove that T. gondii causes unhappiness. Differences in hygiene, food safety, healthcare access, and economic circumstances could influence both infection rates and well-being. After all, health and happiness are difficult to separate from the conditions we live in. Ask anyone who cannot turn on a tap and count on clean, safe water. A parasite may be part of the picture, but so are the everyday resources that help us stay healthy, feel secure, and simply have an easier and more comfortable day-to-day.

T. gondii can spread through undercooked contaminated meat, contaminated soil or produce, water, and accidental ingestion of infectious material from cat feces. Simply petting a cat or sharing a home with one does not automatically cause infection.

Pets can offer us comfort and companionship, but research on pet ownership and mental health has produced mixed results. Benefits vary between individuals, and caring for an animal can also bring financial pressure, stress, disrupted sleep, allergies, property loss or damage, and even grief.

In a recent development, cats are not standardized wellness products with a purring function. Some adore cuddles; others prefer admiration from a respectable distance. A cat who retreats, flattens their ears, or flicks their tail may be asking for space. Ignoring those signs because a human wants affection isn't bonding; it's treating a living, breathing creature like a plush toy.

Good care means respecting those boundaries. Hiding places, elevated resting spots, predictable routines, interactive play, and regular veterinary care all help support feline well-being. Changes in behavior often signal pain or illness, so they deserve attention rather than an automatic label of âbad behavior.â.

According to recent reports, and no, not every cat wants to be carried around like a furry handbag. Some barely tolerate being looked at when they're minding their own business. That's not a character flaw. It's a cat making its position very clear.

The study points to a connection between cat density and national happiness, but it cannot prove that cats make countries happier or that toxoplasmosis explains national differences. The findings raise interesting questions; they don't settle the debate.

In a recent development, for cat families, the practical health advice is simple: litter box hygiene is paramount. Scoop the poop daily, since T. gondii oocysts generally need one to five days after being shed to become infectious. Wash your hands after handling litter, wear gloves while gardening, cook meat thoroughly, and make sure you wash and disinfect fruits and veggies before eating.

In a recent development, pregnant women and those with a weak immune system should consult their doctor about appropriate precautions. During pregnancy, having someone else clean the litter tray is recommended, but a healthy cat should not need to be rehomed because of toxoplasmosis concerns. Good hygiene is more useful than panic.

Industry observers note that ultimately, happiness depends on a complicated mix of economic security, health, social circumstances, and personal relationships. Cats may enrich human lives, but no single animal can explain the mood of an entire nation.

According to recent reports, A familiar purr, a gentle head bump, or a cat choosing your lap to nap in can brighten an ordinary afternoon and put a smile on anyoneâs face. The 3 a.m. bedroom sprints and hairballs left over the Persian rug, however, remain entirely separate research questions!

Industry observers note that “National defense information is classified to protect the American people from bad actors around the world who wish to do us harm,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The details alleged in this affidavit reflect the behavior of a government contractor who exempted himself from a federal law governing the protection of classified information. “Following a referral from the Agency, on Friday, October 23rd, the FBI arrested a contractor who provided services to CIA for alleged unauthorized disclosures of classified information,” remarked CIA Director John Ratcliffe. “The unauthorized release of classified material poses grave risks to our national security, intelligence sources, ongoing operations, and our officers. There is absolutely zero tolerance for leaking, and anyone who violates their oath will be held accountable and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”.

Industry observers note that “As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” noted Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably. Those cleared to hold our Nation's secrets undertake a solemn obligation to protect that information. If proven at trial, this conduct is a grave violation of the Espionage Act, and the National Security Division will prosecute it as such.”.

Ian A. Brinksman, 42, of the District of Columbia was arrested following a search of his residence and charged by criminal complaint with unlawfully transmitting national defense information.

Recent findings suggest that according to the criminal complaint, beginning in 2020, the defendant worked as an employee of a U.S. government agency based in the Eastern District of Virginia and later in 2022 began working as a developer for systems integration for “Tech giant 1,” a contractor to the same U.S. government agency. During all times relevant to the complaint, Brinksman held a Top Secret security clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access.

As further detailed in the complaint, Brinksman had an ongoing personal relationship with an individual who maintains an online publication on Substack (Individual 1). A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 claimed Individual 1 had “published reporting based on classified [relevant U.S. government agency] assessments.” Individual 1 posted on her social media profile, “I also accept leaks.”.

The FBI Chicago Field Office is investigating the case with substantial assistance from the Washington Field Office.

Trial Attorneys Eli Ross and Kathryn DeMarco of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Vito Iaia for the Eastern District of Virginia are prosecuting the case, with valuable assistance from Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tejpal Chawla and Stuart Allen for the District of Columbia.

A female cat suddenly raising her hindquarters into the air, her tail swishing suggestively, can seem like a strange latest behavior. In an unspayed female, though, it's often one of the clearest signs that she's gone into heat.

According to recent reports, heat, more correctly called âestrusâ, is a normal part of a cat's reproductive cycle, but it can bring several noticeable changes in behavior. Unspayed cats typically experience their first heat or season between six and nine months old, although some can start even earlier. After that first season, she will continue to come into heat roughly every 21 days, but during months with longer daylight hours, the cycle can repeat every two to three weeks.

In a recent development, as âlong-dayâ breeders, the female reproductive cycle of cats tends to be linked to warmer seasons when daylight hours are longer. However, depending on the climate and location, they can continue to cycle throughout the year.

Knowing what to look for can make the sudden change in behavior much easier to understand.

The insistent and attention-grabbing raising of the butt is certainly one of the hallmarks of a cat in estrus, but, like with so many feline behaviors, context is key. Here are some classic signs that are commonly â but not exclusively â displayed by a cat in heat.

Industry observers note that the most recognizable behavior is the one that often gets the most attention. A female cat may raise her hindquarters and move her tail off to one side, a posture sometimes described as âpresentingâ.

This is a way for a female to signal to males that she's receptive to mating.

However, the posture by itself doesn't necessarily mean a cat is in heat, and many spayed females, and even male cats, will raise their hindquarters when being petted or while stretching their front legs. It's therefore more useful when considered alongside the other signs of heat.

A raised bum and attentive behavior from a spayed/neutered cat is often a sign of trust and affection.

A cat in heat can become considerably more vocal. The sounds can be loud and intense, and some owners may even mistake the vocalizing for a sign that their cat is in pain.

On its own, though, this behavior isn't usually cause for alarm in a cat that is otherwise showing the typical signs of heat. The vocalizing is part of the way a female calls for a mate.

Frequent vocalizing can have other causes, including illness or pain, so a cat showing additional signs that something isn't right should be checked by a vet.

According to recent reports, rolling around on the floor is hardly unusual for a cat. Cats of either sex may roll around while playing, seeking attention, or scratching an itch.

During heat, however, a female may do it more frequently as part of the behavioral changes that come with her reproductive cycle.

Like raising the hindquarters, rolling isn't enough to confirm that a cat is in heat on its own. It becomes more meaningful when it appears alongside several of the other signs.

Some cats become noticeably more affectionate when they're in heat. They may seek out attention more often, stay close to their owners, or generally seem more interested in interaction than usual.

Recent findings suggest that there are plenty of other reasons a cat might become more affectionate. A cat could be looking for warmth in cold weather or seeking extra attention after being separated from an owner.

That makes increased affection more useful as part of a pattern rather than as a standalone sign.

According to recent reports, urine spraying is more commonly associated with unneutered male cats, but did you know that females can spray too? During heat, the scent is thought to help attract potential mates.

According to recent reports, at the same time, urinating outside the litter box can have many other explanations. Litter box problems, behavioral complications, and medical complications can all cause changes in bathroom habits.

If a cat starts consistently going outside the litter box, it's worth discussing with a vet rather than assuming the behavior is simply related to heat.

Sources indicate that A female cat in heat may become more determined to get outside. Scratching at doors or windows can be part of that behavior, particularly when a cat is trying to find a mate.

Keeping her indoors is especially important during this period. An unspayed female that gets outside has a risk of becoming pregnant, as well as facing the usual dangers associated with roaming, including traffic, animal attacks, and getting lost.

It has been revealed that responsible pet ownership means spaying or neutering your cat. By removing the ovaries and uterus, spaying stops the reproductive cycle permanently, preventing unwanted litters, reducing the risk of uterine infections, and meaningfully lowering the risk of mammary cancer. It also reduces the risks of cats escaping, fighting, and being hit by a car.

There are no health or behavioral advantages to allowing your female cat to have a litter, so veterinary advice is to spay and neuter most cats by 6 months.

Sources indicate that until then, recognizing the signs of heat can make a sudden change in behavior much less confusing. A female cat raising her hindquarters, becoming unusually vocal, rolling around, seeking extra attention, spraying, or trying to get outside may simply be responding to a normal part of her reproductive cycle.

Of course, it may simply be a catâs way of signalling trust and affection!

I purchased my Havanese, Paisley, at 8 weeks. She hasnât eaten any food for three weeks now. That makes her blood sugar drop. I have taken her to the emergency vets twice and my regular vet numerous times.

According to recent reports, they have run multiple liver tests but can't find anything wrong with her. I have been hand-feeding her the prescription sugar water the vet gave me, but I have to force her mouth open to give it to her.

Have you ever heard of anything like this?â.

A tiny puppy has limited energy reserves, so when she stops eating, her blood glucose can fall rapidly. This is one reason we normally feed puppies several times throughout the day. However, three weeks without eating is much more concerning than simple âpuppy hypoglycemia.â Sadly, once a puppy stops eating, this can become a vicious cycle because low blood glucose can cause weakness, abnormal behavior, and even less interest in food. Sugar can temporarily raise her blood glucose, but it does not address the underlying problem. And since Paisley has been refusing food for several weeks, this deserves some serious detective work.

Recent findings suggest that normal liver blood tests are reassuring, but they do not completely rule out every condition that can cause chronic inappetence or recurrent hypoglycemia in a puppy. Depending on what has already been evaluated, your veterinarian may also consider additional investigation for conditions such as infection, gastrointestinal disease, congenital portosystemic shunting, adrenal disease, or other metabolic disorders.

A portosystemic shunt (PSS) is an abnormal blood vessel that allows some blood from the digestive system to bypass the liver instead of passing through it normally. Because the liver plays an key role in processing nutrients and maintaining normal metabolism, this abnormal circulation can cause problems in some puppies. More specialized blood tests and imaging, such as abdominal ultrasound with Doppler evaluation or, in some cases, CT angiography, may be needed to investigate these conditions.

The Havanese is among the breeds with a higher risk of PSS, so if it hasnât already, I think this should be thoroughly investigated.

Although managing her glucose levels is very important, please be cautious;  forcing sugar water into her mouth carries a risk of aspiration (inhaling the liquid into the lungs). If Paisley is conscious and able to swallow normally, the recommendation is to place a small amount of an appropriate glucose source, like the water you mentioned, directly onto her gums or inside her cheek, where it can be absorbed through the mucous membranes. This can help raise her glucose levels without the risk of aspiration. However, if she becomes extremely weak, cannot swallow normally, collapses, becomes unconscious, or has a seizure, nothing should be given by mouth because of the risk of inhaling it into the lungs. Those situations require immediate emergency veterinary treatment.

Because Paisley has gone this long without eating voluntarily and continues to experience low blood glucose, I would discuss referral to a veterinary internal medicine specialist or hospitalization for nutritional and glucose support. Think of the glucose as a power generator keeping the lights on, but the priority is still finding out why the electrical system keeps failing. Sugar can keep the lights on for a while, but eventually we need to find the faulty wiring. Supporting her blood glucose is essential, but identifying and treating the underlying cause is what will ultimately allow her to maintain normal glucose without constant intervention.

I wish you and Paisley the very best, and I hope this helps.

Letâs Be S.M.A.R.T. in Keratea, Greece, is a truly unique organization, currently home to over 100 cats and 13 dogs, living in a cage-free, home-like, villa-style environment. S.M.A.R.T. stands for Successfully Managing Animal Rights Today, and for Julie Kelley, founder and manager of this international animal welfare organization, that means working towards global animal welfare, sharing essential information and facts about animals worldwide, and helping people understand the benefits that come from treating animals with compassion and care.

I had been traveling to Greece since 1998 and would see the issues with stray cats and dogs. I felt very comfortable in Greece. I had business with Greek nationals in New York, learned a lot of the language, and understood the cultural differences. I felt it was my mission to create Letâs Be S.M.A.R.T. to help people understand the great benefits animals provide to us humans and to educate young people as well. Of course, after a couple of years, it was hard not to take in the first kitty who gave birth, and well, it just grew exponentially from there! Since 2007, we have added many programs and special projects to continue our quest to provide the best we can for our strays.

According to recent reports, letâs be S.M.A.R.T. aims to educate the public about the importance of animals by raising awareness of their rights, well-being, and care. We believe in thinking globally and acting locally by supporting special projects as they arise and, through our programs, bringing communities together to promote responsible animal care.

In Greece, our campaign is primarily centred on reducing the suffering, abuse, and neglect of animals while increasing public awareness of their needs and rights. These include running an innovative and modern foster home, managing a rehoming program for rescued animals, and collaborating with municipalities to implement effective stray animal care initiatives. We also provide practical solutions for supporting strays in urban communitiesâsuch as ensuring access to food and waterâand we actively engage philanthropic individuals who travel to Greece to volunteer, learn about shelter medicine, and receive training in best practices in animal care.

The creation of the sanctuary and setting up the organization in Greece was a huge accomplishment. Let's be S.M.A.R.T. is always evolving with fresh ideas to make life better for the cats and dogs we have in our care.

Our campaign model is unique in Greece. We have created the âSMART Starfish approachâ in which all five arms must function together to create the best outcome.

Each arm of the starfish represents a core pillar of our mission:.

Sterilization â controlling population growth at its source.

Medical Care & Microchipping â restoring health and identity.

Feeding & Shelter â stability, nourishment, and safety.

Education & Community â knowledge that shapes future behavior.

NGO Collaboration â collective strength through partnership.

For years, our programs and ideas have been influencing how animal charities operate and making permanent changes for a better future for animal welfare in Greece.

Industry observers note that we created the following programs: Volunteer, SMART Family Video Series, Veterinary Internship, SMART Yards, and Adoption Vacation, all of which are operational every day and are detailed on the Programs page on our website, if you would like to take a closer look. We could not function without the help of our amazing Volunteers.

Industry observers note that we successfully found wonderful homes for 73 cats in 2025. I'm not 100% sure, but I would say we are one of the leading cat adopters in Greece!

Sources indicate that we receive multiple enquiries from tourists who have found a cat or kitten, and they want to take it home with them to their country. Many times they have cared for them during their stay, provided medicine, bottle-fed babies, etc. This has become increasingly common, with visitors seeing cats all over Greece. Therefore, I decided to offer the Adoption-Vacation as a package. We care for the kitten or cat until it is ready to travel, taking care of the necessary vaccines, passport, microchip, etc. Once the cat is ready to travel, we make travel arrangements with the adopter.

You can see our cats, kittens, and dogs for adoption on our website and have a video chat with us about your requirements and meet a cat if you have already fallen in love (we created a Kitty Picker to help you choose the character of your cat), and then arrange a visit with us when you arrive in Greece. If the home check is secured, we arrange the papers for your new pet to travel home with you. Or we can foster a cat you rescue while you are in Greece and deal with the veterinary needs, papers etc. The cat can travel after you leave with a flight buddy or one of our volunteers.

What better souvenir to have from Greece than a beautiful cat that needed special love and care?

It has been revealed that everything we do is linked. The more sterilizations we achieve, the safer and healthier the animals are in the community; they are interacting better with each other, and people know they are sterilized.

We would like the municipalities and communities all over Greece to enjoy the benefits of the SMART Yards and help take care of the animals. Working together is the future. We are also collaborating with some officials regarding some policies involving the strays and to help create some standards for housing the strays. Animals and people need to coexist in a humane way. Not every cat needs to be inside a home but can remain cared for and part of our ecosystem.

A rather big goal is to find someone to help us purchase the property we rent, make refurbishments and sustainable features, and add a vet clinic for shared use with other charities and our vet interns. This is a tall order, but we are looking for someone who would like to leave a legacy.

We also want to extend our ability to provide food and shelter after sterilization so that every animal is cared for.

Our animals live in a home-style environment, so every day is the same as if they were living in a family home. Cats are either in bedrooms; we have a retirement room, a special dietary needs room, and a kitten nursery, each with cats that are selected to share a room together, or they are in the main house and free to mingle and hang out on our netted balconies in cute wooden houses and take in the fresh air and nature, since we are in a rural setting, just 15 minutes from Athens International Airport.

It has been revealed that some of the funniest moments are with kittens and playful cats. Plus, bonded pairs â we have a husband-and-wife team called Jasper and Margot who need to be adopted together, and they are very entertaining with their games and spats.

Cats and dogs choose who they like and want to go home with. We find people fall in love with cats that come to them, and a chemistry is formed. Sometimes a visitor leaves, and they cannot stop thinking about the cat they fell in love with and make an application to adopt. We are so happy when this happens. We have repeat adoptions from families and visitors all over the world. We also have Sponsors and Patreon for people to support our work.

Recent findings suggest that volunteering is open to everyone around the world who would like to come to stay and help us. If you love animals, it's an opportunity to help save lives. It's pure joy to see a cat or dog that was sick transform into good health and finally live in a wonderful family home. That's what the team at Let's be S.M.A.R.T. wants for them all: to be safe, healthy, and happy.

It has been revealed that people can also help by following, subscribing, and sharing us on socials. Donations are greatly appreciated, as are supplies, and we created the Amazon Wishlist so gifts can be sent to us directly from Amazon Germany, tax-free.

Sources indicate that if youâre visiting Greece and see a lot of stray cats, itâs a good idea to ask around if there is a local organization helping to take care of them. If you see an injured cat, you should immediately try to find a responsible person or contact the local police.

You can also post on local social media groups to try to find help. Most of the cats we take into our foster home settings are from tourists or residents who find our website through a Google search. It is hard to avoid helping, but I would suggest not removing an animal from their setting to a hotel room or Airbnb, and then leaving and putting it back on the street. The cat can get disoriented and perhaps be in danger.

We truly hope to have more controlled community care for our strays in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artem Stryzhak, 36, a Ukrainian national, was sentenced today to 70 months in prison for conspiracy to commit computer fraud in connection with a series of ransomware attacks that targeted hospitals, government entities, law firms, and other businesses around the world.

It has been revealed that “This sentence concludes a years-long, multi-continent investigation into a defendant who participated in cyber-attacks against Americans’ businesses and health care,” remarked Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Cybercriminals who terrorize American businesses cannot evade justice by operating from abroad or hiding behind sophisticated technology. Artem Stryzhak’s sentence underscores the Justice Department’s resolve to dismantle ransomware groups, hold them accountable, and protect American businesses and people from cyber extortion.”.

According to recent reports, “Ransomware attacks like those committed by the defendant wreak enormous havoc — harming victim companies that pay millions in remediation and ransoms, preventing hospitals and other critical facilities from accessing data, and putting sensitive information in the hands of bad actors,” noted U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of Fresh York. “Today’s sentence reflects that cybercriminals cannot hide from law enforcement and will face significant punishment for their criminal conduct. We remain determined to capture Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, a serial ransomware developer and Stryzhak’s co-conspirator.”.

In a recent development, “Disrupting a ransomware group that attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide and sentencing a defendant who had targeted healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic is of significant importance to this office,” mentioned U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe for the Middle District of Florida. “We are proud of our law enforcement partners for their skilled investigative work in bringing this criminal to justice.”.

Sources indicate that “Artem Stryzhak is a prolific cybercriminal who worked with multiple ransomware groups to target U.S. businesses and hospitals,” stated Operations Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Branch. “These groups disrupted patient care and caused more than $100 million in losses. Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak’s crimes and demonstrates the FBI’s global reach and extensive network of international partners. Multiple field offices contributed to this investigation, and our work does not end here. We will continue to leverage every tool at our disposal to track down Stryzhak’s co-conspirators and hold them accountable, including Volodymyr Viktorovych Tymoshchuk.”.

Industry observers note that according to court documents, Stryzhak, formerly of Barcelona, Spain, conspired with others to perpetrate ransomware attacks on behalf of multiple ransomware groups against victim computer networks in the United States and other countries. The conspiracies caused significant damage to victim computer systems. Beginning in approximately June 2021, Stryzhak joined the ongoing Nefilim conspiracy as a Nefilim ransomware affiliate. Stryzhak was given access to the Nefilim ransomware and agreed with one of the Nefilim ransomware group administrators, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, to pay the Nefilim administrators, including Tymoshchuk, 20% of the ransom proceeds extorted from victims in exchange for Stryzhak’s access to the Nefilim ransomware.

The ransomware attacks that Stryzhak conducted with Nefilim ransomware included a June 2021 attack in which Stryzhak stole data from a firm in the oil and gas transportation industry. About a week later, Stryzhak created email addresses that were incorporated in a ransom note sent to the victim company. Stryzhak conspired with the Nefilim ransomware actors until at least October 2021. If a victim paid the ransom demand, the perpetrators provided the decryption key, enabling the victim to decrypt files locked by the ransomware.

Also according to court documents, Stryzhak separately joined the Hive ransomware group as one of its earliest affiliates. From June 2021 to January 2023, Hive conspirators attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide, including government entities, hospitals, and businesses. Hive ransomware attacks caused major disruptions in victim daily operations around the world and affected responses to the COVID-19 pandemic. In one case, a hospital attacked by the Hive ransomware group had to forgo digital technology to treat existing patients and was unable to accept upcoming patients immediately following the attack.

Sources indicate that in his role as a Hive affiliate, Stryzhak and his co-conspirators deployed Hive ransomware against seven victims, including law firms, a dentist office, and a healthcare provider during the COVID-19 pandemic. Victims were unable to access their encrypted data. The FBI, as part of a months-long disruption campaign against the Hive ransomware group, provided a decryption key to one of Stryzhak’s victims, thereby allowing that victim to decrypt its encrypted data without having to pay a ransom.

According to recent reports, stryzhak was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the United States in April 2025. Stryzhak pleaded guilty in December 2025 to two counts of conspiracy to commit fraud, extortion, and related activity in connection with computers.

Sources indicate that the FBI Springfield Field Office investigated the Nefilim ransomware case and the FBI Tampa Field Office investigated the Hive ransomware case. The Criminal Division’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI’s New York Field Office, and Spanish law enforcement authorities provided substantial assistance locating, arresting, and extraditing Stryzhak.

Acting Assistant Deputy Chief James S. Yoon of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), former CCIPS Senior Trial Attorney Brian Z. Mund, and Assistant United States Attorneys Alexander F. Mindlin and Ellen H. Sise of the Eastern District of New York’s National Security and Cybercrime Section prosecuted the Nefilim ransomware case. CCIPS Trial Attorneys Alison M. Zitron and Christen M. Gallagher and Assistant United States Attorney Hannah Watson of the Middle District of Florida prosecuted the Hive ransomware case.

Sources indicate that the U.S. Department of State’s Transnational Organized Crime (TOC) Rewards Program has offered a reward of up to $11 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction or location of Stryzhak’s charged co-conspirator, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk. Anyone with information about Tymoshchuk should contact the FBI via phone at +1-917-242-1407, by email at TymoTips@fbi.gov, by contacting your local field office, if in the United States, or by contacting the nearest U.S. Embassy, if located overseas. More information about the Tymoshchuk TOC reward offer and one related to Hive ransomware is located on the State Department website.

CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.

  • Recent findings suggest that A dog's breath is never going to be minty fresh, but there's a big difference between ordinary doggy breath and an odor that's genuinely foul.
  • Bad breath can have several possible causes, ranging from common dental problems to health conditions that need urgent veterinary attention.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that dogster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn a commission at no cost to you. Read about privacy.

Recent findings suggest that A dog's breath is never going to be minty fresh, but there's a big difference between ordinary doggy breath and an odor that's genuinely foul. A healthy dog's mouth should have a mild smell, often with a faint trace of whatever they last ate. When that smell suddenly becomes fishy, rotten, or unusually unpleasant, it can be a sign that something else is going on.

Bad breath can have several possible causes, ranging from common dental problems to health conditions that need urgent veterinary attention. Knowing what that smell might be telling you can make it easier to recognize when it's time for a closer look.

Periodontal disease is the most common cause of persistent bad breath in dogs. It develops as tartar builds up on the teeth and eventually affects the ligament holding each tooth in place.

The smell can become particularly strong and rotten as the disease progresses. Other signs include inflamed or bleeding gums, loose or missing teeth, heavy tartar, exposed tooth roots, changes in appetite, difficulty chewing, and pawing at the mouth.

According to recent reports, gingivitis is an earlier stage of periodontal disease and causes the gums to become inflamed. Bad breath is often one of the first noticeable signs.

It has been revealed that unlike more advanced periodontal disease, gingivitis is reversible when treated. A professional dental cleaning combined with regular dental care at home can usually address the problem. Without treatment, however, gingivitis can progress into periodontal disease and eventually contribute to tooth loss.

Sometimes the mouth isn't where the problem starts. Digestive conditions can also affect the way a dog's breath smells.

Sources indicate that gastroenteritis, acid reflux, food intolerances, intestinal blockages, and even gastrointestinal cancer can all be associated with changes in breath odor. Many of these conditions can cause vomiting, which leaves behind a sharp, sour smell from bile.

Acid reflux can also produce a similar sour odor even when a dog isn't actually vomiting.

What a dog eats can have a noticeable effect on breath. It's perfectly normal for some of the smell of a dog's food to linger after a meal, but certain diets can leave a much stronger odor behind.

Seafood and fish oil supplements, for example, can give a dog's breath a distinctly fishy smell. Dogs that eat feces, whether their own or another animal's, can also develop particularly foul breath afterward. This behavior, known as coprophagia, is unpleasant but fairly common.

Bad breath isn't always caused by the teeth or gums. The oral cavity also includes the jaw bones, tongue, soft palate, and the inside of the cheeks, and problems affecting any of these areas can produce an unpleasant smell.

Recent findings suggest that injuries can become infected and lead to tissue damage, creating the odor associated with the breakdown of damaged tissue. Tumors can also develop in these areas and may cause similar tissue damage and bad breath.

A sweet or fruity smell coming from a dog's breath can have a very different explanation. In a diabetic dog, it can be a sign of ketoacidosis, a serious complication that occurs when the body doesn't have enough insulin and begins burning fat for energy instead.

According to recent reports, this process produces ketones, which can become toxic as they accumulate in the blood. The resulting breath can have a sweet, fruity smell that is sometimes compared with acetone.

Interestingly, not everyone can smell ketones on a dog's breath. Differences in how people perceive smells, including genetic differences in scent perception, may explain why the odor is more noticeable to some people than others.

Kidney disease can give a dog's breath a distinct ammonia-like smell.

In a recent development, healthy kidneys filter waste products such as urea from the bloodstream so they can be removed from the body through urine. When kidney function is impaired, urea can build up in the blood instead.

That excess urea eventually reacts with saliva and converts to ammonia, producing the distinctive smell that can be noticeable on a dog's breath.

An unpleasant smell coming from a dog's mouth doesn't always originate anywhere near the mouth. In fact, the problem could be at the opposite end!

Impacted or infected anal glands can cause a dog to lick or nibble the area in an attempt to relieve the discomfort. Anal gland fluid often has an intensely fishy smell, and when a dog licks the area, that odor can transfer directly to the mouth and breath.

Persistent bad breath is worth investigating rather than simply trying to cover up the smell. The underlying cause could be as manageable as dental disease, but it can also be associated with more serious health problems.

Regular brushing and professional dental cleanings can help prevent periodontal disease, which is the most common cause of ongoing bad breath in dogs.

According to recent reports, A sudden change in breath odor deserves particular attention, especially if it appears alongside other changes such as appetite problems, vomiting, or repeated licking at a particular part of the body. In those situations, a vet can help determine what's causing the smell and whether anything else needs to be treated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Department of Justice revealed today that it has entered into a non-prosecution agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc.
  • The Department reached the agreement under its 2026 Corporate Enforcement and Voluntary Self-Disclosure Policy (“the Policy”), which incentivizes companies to voluntarily disclose discovered misconduct, cooperate with Department investigations, and timely and appropriately remediate the wrongdoing.
  • This agreement with Extreme Networks marks the Department’s first non-prosecution agreement in a “near-miss” case under the Policy, meaning a case that involved full cooperation and appropriate remediation but did not qualify for a declination of prosecution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Department of Justice revealed today that it has entered into a non-prosecution agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. The company agreed to pay criminal penalties totaling $975,721.84 to resolve the Department’s investigation of sanctions and export control offenses.

The Department reached the agreement under its 2026 Corporate Enforcement and Voluntary Self-Disclosure Policy (“the Policy”), which incentivizes companies to voluntarily disclose discovered misconduct, cooperate with Department investigations, and timely and appropriately remediate the wrongdoing.

This agreement with Extreme Networks marks the Department’s first non-prosecution agreement in a “near-miss” case under the Policy, meaning a case that involved full cooperation and appropriate remediation but did not qualify for a declination of prosecution. While Extreme Networks’ disclosure to the National Security Division (NSD) was not timely because it occurred under imminent threat of disclosure by a news publication, Extreme Networks nonetheless fully cooperated with the Department’s investigation and timely and appropriately remediated the misconduct. As a result, its disclosure qualified as a “Near Miss” Voluntary Self-Disclosure under the Policy.

“This non-prosecution agreement and million-dollar criminal penalty mark the successful resolution of our investigation into the illegal sale of advanced networking equipment and services to a Russian weapons manufacturer, in clear violation of U.S. sanctions and export controls,” mentioned Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “The FBI remains dedicated to keeping sensitive technology out of the hands of the Russian military, and we're grateful to Homeland Security Investigations and the Bureau of Industry and Security for their partnership on this case. Let this announcement serve as a clear warning: if you attempt to arm our adversaries by violating U.S. law, justice will find you.”.

Recent findings suggest that “HSI remains committed to investigating companies and individuals who evade U.S. export controls and sanctions to provide goods or services to foreign weapons manufacturers,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Pierczynski of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Detroit. “These laws protect our national security and prevent U.S.-origin products and services from supporting adversaries’ military capabilities. HSI will continue working with our law enforcement and regulatory partners to identify and hold accountable those who undermine these critical safeguards.”.

The agreement arose out of an investigation into Extreme Networks’ sales of products and services to Moscow Machinery Building Plant Avangard (MMZA), a Russian weapons manufacturer that was owned by JSC Concern Almaz-Antey (Almaz Antey), which was added to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List by the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in July 2014.

Industry observers note that pursuant to the non-prosecution agreement, Extreme Networks will forfeit $487,860.92 in proceeds from the sanctions and export control offenses and pay a criminal fine of $487,860.92, for a total criminal penalty of $975,721.84. Extreme Networks will also resolve a parallel administrative action by OFAC.

Recent findings suggest that between around March 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks, through its then-Russia based subsidiary, Extreme Networks Rus LLC, processed and fulfilled 11 purchase orders for networking equipment and services to MMZA without the required license or authorization from OFAC. MMZA was a primary producer of the S-300 and S-400 anti-aircraft missile systems used by the Russian army. To facilitate these sales, certain Russia-based Extreme Networks employees concealed the identity of MMZA from Extreme Networks’ global trade compliance group, causing Extreme Networks to file false electronic export information via the Automated Export System and smuggle goods from the United States. Through this scheme, Extreme Networks deprived the U.S. government of its ability to carry out its lawful function of enforcing sanctions and export controls designed to protect national security and economic interests. As a result of its unlawful conduct, Extreme Networks earned approximately $487,860.92 in revenue from the sales of goods and services.

According to recent reports, although Extreme Networks’ self-disclosure to NSD was not timely pursuant to the Policy, Extreme Networks nonetheless cooperated with the Department’s investigation by timely providing relevant facts and documents and making employees available for interviews. Extreme Networks also appropriately remediated the misconduct by terminating its contract with the third-party distributor it used to facilitate these sales, improving screening procedures, hiring additional compliance personnel, and implementing diligence procedures in connection with mergers and acquisitions. Given these steps and the lack of aggravating circumstances, the Department agreed to enter into a non-prosecution agreement.

The FBI Charlotte Field Office, the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security, and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case.

According to recent reports, this case was prosecuted by former Trial Attorney Maria Fedor of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Adam Hulbig for the Eastern District of North Carolina.

Please see the Justice Department’s policy here.

Meet Dave Coverly, creator of the popular cartoon panel, âSpeed Bumpâ, which appears internationally in hundreds of publications, including The Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, and the Detroit Free Press. His work was named âBest in Newspaper Panelsâ by the National Cartoonists Society in 1995, 2003, 2014, and 2021. He is also the principal cartoonist for Bark (formerly BarkBox) and illustrator for Ranger Rick magazine.

We sit down with Dave to learn the story behind his charmingly wry comic, and find out how, 32 years down the road, inspiration in the ordinary keeps his content relevant and relatable.

The path to becoming a professional cartoonist always starts in childhood â pretty much every kid likes to draw, right? And I was no different. But as kids get older, they tend to get more particular about how good their drawings look, and thatâs where frustration sets in. They tend to move on to other hobbies. Where a cartoonistâs path diverges from that of wiser, more sensible humans is that we love the process of creating more than we chafe at the frustration. Believe me, there is frustration. One misconception about artists is that we do it because it comes easy to us, but the general truth is that most of us put in long hours because we want to be good at what we already love.

I taped rejection letters to the wall above my drawing table for motivation. At the time, though, my panels didnât have a title, so when my breakthrough finally happened, I needed to name it. I submitted a list of possible titles to Creators, and Speed Bump was the unanimous choice. Fortunately, that was my top choice, too. Iâd like people to perhaps slow down just for a second when they read my work since Iâm rarely going to hit you over the head with the joke.

My second favorite title was The Wide World of Stretch Pants.

In a recent development, animal humor has always been a part of my work. I was slightly obsessed with Ranger Rick magazine growing up, and spent loads of time drawing the critters they featured. I discovered thereâs something inherently funny and absurd about talking animals, not to mention itâs the most fun way to trigger the imagination. What would a giraffe order at a restaurant? What does a dolphin dream about? That was how I discovered how much fun cartooning was â and that the crazier you make it, the less perfect it needs to be.

It has been revealed that iâve always had a dog until very recently, and had two hilarious knuckleheads as a kid: Shag and Tigger. They were actually father and son, and I didnât need a DNA test to prove it â Shag got out one day, and the neighborhood kids on bikes came by to let me know he could be found down the street at Queenieâs house, where they were in the front yard together. Letâs just say Shag was living up to his name. Then Queenie begat Tigger.

I grew up in a small lake community, but Shag was found by my grandpa just living on the streets of Detroit. He was pretty feral â Shag, not my grandpa â and impossible to train, but also a total sweetheart. They slept in the garage, and in the morning weâd often find him sleeping on top of the car. Tigger, on the other hand, preferred to sleep behind the toilet. And he wasnât a small dog.

In any case, I believe these two funny mutts had as much influence on my work as any other cartoonist.

Sources indicate that great question! Cats and dogs are obviously very different, but they have one really significant thing in common: their own unique personalities. Thatâs what makes both perfect for cartoons â most of us already treat them like little furry people anyway, right? Itâs just their behaviors that set them apart.

Dogs tend to be goofier, cats tend to be cooler, and they show affection in their own ways, too. Pets generate a lot of material because almost everyone knows a dog or a cat. Even if they donât have one (or many) themselves, the odds are a reader will recognize why the cartoon is funny (hopefully!).

One of my most popular cartoons is a sign that says âBeware of Avant-Guard Dog,â and the dog in the yard is wearing black and a beret and holding a sign simply saying WOOF. The idea started as a pun, but I think one of the reasons readers seem to like it so much is that it plays against type. The dogâs sensibility is quite cat-like, making it even more absurd.

My new book is a full-color collection of the âbest ofâ my dog cartoons from the last decade, and thereâs only one cartoon per page so that they can be seen in a larger format, which was important to me. I put a lot of effort into the art and the details, things that are often lost when the cartoons are shrunk down to an illegible size, so I wanted readers to be able to fully enjoy that aspect of the cartoons. Also, the friend who colors my panels, Ron Raff, is a genius, so whether you think the jokes are funny or not, youâll see that they look gorgeous and consistent throughout!

It was difficult but fun to choose which cartoons made the cut, too. Some are simply personal favorites; others were chosen based on readersâ reactions and how much love they got online. Feedback is extremely helpful, by the way â sometimes it feels like Iâm drawing these alone in my belfry studio and tossing them into a black hole, so hearing from people which ones they liked really makes my day.

In a recent development, there are two aspects to dog cartoons: The first and most obvious is that they really arejokes about dogsâ behavior in general â how they eat, how they might react in different settings, why they lick themselves, bathroom habits, etc etc. Thereâs a lot of material there! The second aspect is what generates even more material, and thatâs when dogs are reflecting human behavior, or simply behaving like a human.

Many of the dog cartoons are really about us, and heaven knows people will never stop providing fodder for jokes. Dogs â and animals in general â are a good buffer between the joke and the point of the joke. A good example in the book is a dog shaking a toy in his mouth, and a woman next to him is saying, âBad dog! Drop Mommyâs voodoo doll! Bad dog!â In the background, her husband (presumably) shakes back and forth like the toy. At some level, the cartoon is about the coupleâs relationship, right? But itâs framed by a typical and humorous dog action weâve all seen before. Just not with a voodoo doll, haha.

According to recent reports, I would say simply that our question is also the answer: love. I try to approach my cartoons the same way I approach dogs in real life; from a standpoint of love, affection, admiration, and a little bit of gratitude that they exist.

Industry observers note that there have been too many to count over three decades! I drew a cartoon years ago of a man walking his dog in heaven, but the leash is attached to the dogâs halo. A few weeks later, I received a card in the mail from a woman whose dog had just passed awayâ¦only a month after her husband. She said she cried with happiness thinking of the two of them like that, and it made her heart feel lighter. How incredibly moving is that? I think of that often: when I share a cartoon, the reader brings their own life experiences to it and then weâve made a two-way connection. That connection is my favorite part of the gig.

According to recent reports, my only hope is that my cartoons help people simply see the world in a different way for a few seconds. I want them to laugh with others and not at others; see that absurdities are universal and that when we recognize ourselves or others in a cartoon, weâre really just acknowledging that weâre all connected.

And then I hope they cut them out and slap them on their fridges.

Sources indicate that adopting can be one of the most rewarding ways to welcome a new pet into your life. But for many would-be adopters, the biggest hurdle isnât necessarily that they don't want to adopt; it's feeling confident that theyâre making an informed and responsible decision.

It has been revealed that mars research found that while 58% of pet owners have never adopted from a shelter or rescue organization, nearly a third would consider it with the right support available. Whether you have concerns about a pet's medical and behavior history, or understanding what to feed them, there are lots of questions to consider before welcoming a upcoming dog into your home.

Mars is #ClearingThePath to pet adoption by giving prospective and latest dog owners access to practical, expert-backed support throughout the journey.

Responsible adoption is about more than picking the right dog; it's about making sure you can realistically meet their needs. Before adopting, think about your living space, daily routine, work arrangements, and how much time you can dedicate to helping your fresh dog settle in and meeting their exercise, enrichment, and training needs.

Recent findings suggest that surprising for some, living in an apartment, for example, does not automatically mean you cannot adopt a dog. The right match depends less on the size of your home and more on whether you can meet that individual dogâs physical, mental, and social needs.

Industry observers note that always mention if you have existing pets or children at the beginning of the adoption process too. Shelter staff can help identify pets whose personality, energy level, and other needs may be a good fit for family life.

The more you speak honestly and openly with the shelter about your home, family, and daily routine, the more they can help you understand which dog will be the right match.

Moving from a shelter into a home is a huge change for your new best friend, and youâd be amazed by how many dogs are returned to shelters within their first few days, before theyâve even had a chance to decompress, let alone adjust to their new situation.

A useful way to think about the transition is the â3-3-3â guideline: the first three days, three weeks, and three months.

Sources indicate that during the first three days, your dog may feel overwhelmed. Dogs may hide, sleep more than usual, show less interest in food, or simply seem unsure of their surroundings. Some dogs may even show signs of fear or defensiveness, and itâs crucial to understand that this is not necessarily their true personality.

Keep things calm and predictable, and let your dog set the pace.

Recent findings suggest that once they become more comfortable, you may start seeing more of their personality from around three weeks, and this can be a good time to introduce gentle routines, socialization, and basic training. By around three months, many dogs may feel much more at home, although every pet is different, so donât worry if your dog seems to need longer. Just be patient and give them the time and space they need to feel safe.

Mars research found that 71% of adopters change their petâs diet immediately after adoption. However, switching your upcoming dogâs food right away may not be the best option, even if their previous diet wasnât the best quality. Ask the shelter what your dog at the moment eats, how much they are fed, and how often. Keeping their existing food and routine initially can help reduce unnecessary disruption.

If you want to change their food, wait a week or so to allow them to adjust, then do so gradually by adding a small proportion of the new diet to the dogâs regular diet. On the first day, their old food should make up around three-quarters of the meal, with the new food making up the rest.

Puppies in particular need age-appropriate nutrition to support growth and should not be switched onto adult food too early.

A dogâs diet should be complete and balanced for their age, size, activity level, body condition and health needs, and plenty of fresh water should always be available.

Consistency can help your dog understand their latest environment and build trust.

According to recent reports, establish regular times for meals, walks, rest, and play. As your dog becomes more comfortable, you can begin introducing basic training using positive reinforcement. Keep sessions short, fun, and rewarding.

Itâs normal for there to be some bumps along the way as your dog adjusts to a fresh home and routine. Behaviors they had previously learned â toilet training, for example â may temporarily change while they settle in, so patience and consistency are key.

If you notice any sudden, persistent, or concerning changes in behavior, speak to your veterinarian or a qualified behavior professional for advice.

Recent findings suggest that adopting and bringing a upcoming dog home is just the beginning, and itâs completely normal for questions to come up as they settle into a new routine. If you need extra guidance regarding their behavior, health, nutrition, or day-to-day care, donât be afraid to reach out. Your shelter, veterinarian, or a qualified behavior professional can help you understand the right way forward.

My 1-year-old cat Daisy has allergies. She is on a special hydrolyzed diet. Iâm trying to find an allergen-neutralizing spray to cut back on dust mites in the house. Would you recommend any specific products?

In a recent development, since Daisy is already on a hydrolyzed diet, it makes sense to look at environmental allergens too, especially if her allergic signs are continuing. Dust mites are common household allergens, and while the goal is to reduce the amount of allergens in her environment, eliminating them completely is not realistic. Regularly washing bedding and blankets, vacuuming with a HEPA filter, and keeping dust to a minimum are still the best places to start.

According to recent reports, if you would like to try a spray, Purefy Anti-Allergen Spray works differently from an insecticide. It is intended to neutralize or remove the allergenic proteins associated with dust mite debris, particularly the proteins found in their feces and other microscopic particles that accumulate in household dust and fabrics. Those proteins, rather than the living mite itself, are an notable source of the allergic reaction. So the idea is not to kill every mite in the house, but to reduce the allergen they leave behind.

I would specifically avoid routinely using insecticide or acaricide sprays around Daisy, even when a product is marketed as ânatural.â Cats can be particularly sensitive to certain botanical ingredients and insecticides, including some essential oils and pyrethroids. If you use an anti-allergen spray, follow the label carefully, keep Daisy away from treated surfaces until they are completely dry, ventilate the area well, and never spray it directly on her or on surfaces she is likely to lick. Please ensure you also keep it away from food and water bowls.

According to recent reports, think of the spray as an extra layer of environmental control, not a treatment for Daisy's allergy. The unglamorous combination of washing, HEPA vacuuming, and reducing dust is still doing most of the heavy lifting. And if Daisy continues to have significant allergic signs despite a properly conducted hydrolyzed diet trial and environmental management, it is worth investigating other possible triggers rather than simply reaching for stronger household chemicals. Usually, the answer is not a more powerful spray, but figuring out exactly what is making your cat itchy. So, real detective work is often needed for success.
